verdict.line: You win if you force extended trades before level 6 while his Q stacks are low; you lose if he farms safely, hits his ultimate on cooldown, and snowballs stacks into the late game.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire kit is built around Siphoning Strike (Q) permanently growing in power off kills, and that ability only reaches 255 range, so his lane strength is capped by how safely he's allowed to farm. Yorick's Q (Last Rites) sustain and W (Dark Procession) wall let him force extended trades that Nasus can't easily walk away from before level 6. The matchup sits at 47.9% over 1384 games because Nasus's level 6 power spike and late-game stack snowball claw back whatever early lane and solo-kill edge Yorick holds.

theirWindow.what: His R (Fury of the Sands) grants bonus health, extended attack range, and drains your max health into bonus damage for its duration. Disengage instead of extending a trade here unless you can close it out immediately.

yourWindow.what: Use your Q (Last Rites) sustain and W (Dark Procession) wall to force extended trades he can't walk away from, since Siphoning Strike's 255 range leaves him nothing to poke you with from range. This is where your lane and solo-kill advantage is strongest.

start.why: Highest-performing start (48.6% over 827 games); the extra sustain and damage matter because you want to win short trades inside his 255-range Q before he can pull ahead on stacks.

boots.why: Most-picked and highest win rate boots (49.2% over 772 games); Nasus's trading pattern is auto-attack heavy once Soul Eater is stacking lifesteal, and flat damage reduction blunts that.

runes.keystoneWhy: Highest win-rate page here (44.9% over tracked games); the free healthbar advantage from proc'ing it on him every trade matters directly against a champion whose own kit has no sustain outside stacked Soul Eater lifesteal.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked combo (39.8%) and the better-performing standard page (49.3%); Ignite converts your solo-kill advantage into an actual kill instead of letting him walk away to heal off Soul Eater.

playing.title: Fight inside his 255 range
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike (Q) only reaches 255 units, so holding melee range forces Nasus to commit to trades on your terms instead of poking safely from outside it.

playing.title: Track his Q stack count
playing.detail: Every kill with Siphoning Strike (Q) permanently increases its damage, so if he's missed CS or been shoved off the wave, he's under-stacked and winnable fights get easier.

playing.title: Wall him when he retreats
playing.detail: Drop W (Dark Procession) to block his retreat path once a trade turns in your favor, since you hold the solo-kill advantage and want to finish fights rather than let him reset.

playing.title: Mark before you commit
playing.detail: Open extended trades with E (Mourning Mist) to shred armor and slow him, then follow with Q (Last Rites) for bonus damage and healing on a 6-4s cooldown as you level.

playing.title: Respect the exact level 6 spike
playing.detail: The moment Nasus hits level 6, his R (Fury of the Sands) grants bonus health, range, and drains your max health into damage for its duration; don't extend a trade there without a clear kill.

playing.title: Dig graves even in losing trades
playing.detail: Any Q (Last Rites) cast on a champion target digs a grave regardless of outcome, so even a trade you lose still feeds your Mist Walker count for the next skirmish.

playing.title: Step out of Spirit Fire zones
playing.detail: His E (Spirit Fire) is a stationary zone on a 12s cooldown that damages you and reduces your armor while you stand in it; don't facetank CS through it when you can path around.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the tactical reading of ranges, cooldowns, and timing windows is my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Try to fight Nasus whenever possible. If he tries to escape by using (W), trap him inside [W] to chase him.
